subject: Post-call: Acme performance & concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limit options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Acme performance & concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limit options

Hi Liam / Rahul \u0014

Thanks again for the call today \u0014 good discussion. Quick recap + two asks so we can put together a recommended config and a pilot quota:\u2028

Summary of requirements from today’s call:
- Latency SLO: P95 generation latency <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). For longer generations we expect streaming; overall interactive UX target is sub-500ms first-byte for streaming start.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 req/s during business hours, with predictable daytime bursts up to ~1,200 req/s (10\u001315 minute spikes).
- Concurrency: logical concurrency target is 400 parallel active requests for our main chat endpoint. Sustained concurrency across the fleet could hit 600 during heavier days.
- Streaming: required for >512-token generations. Need chunked streaming and client connection keep-alive.
- Connection pooling: prefer long-lived HTTP/1.1 keep-alive or HTTP/2 multiplexing from our edge; connection churn should be minimal.

What I need from you to finalize a recommendation:
1) Can you confirm the % of requests that are <256 tokens vs >512 tokens and an example 95th percentile response size? A sample (anonymized) 1-hour export would be ideal \u0014 attached is a template.
2) Is a 30-day canary pilot with a temporary quota increase acceptable to validate tail latency under your burst profile?

Next steps on our side: I’ll loop in engineering (cc’d Stephanie) to propose a Dedicated/reserved concurrency configuration and a temporary rate-limit/quota plan that maps to your spike profile. I’ll include cost estimates and a suggested rollout (canary -> scale). Attached: redwood-slo-options.pdf \u0014 initial options and trade-offs (reserved concurrency, burst capacity, per-minute rate limits).

If helpful we can do a short sync with your infra team to walk through connection pooling/keep-alive settings (we've seen many customers get large wins by switching to HTTP/2).

Thanks \u0014 talk soon.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-slo-options.pdf, acme-request-patterns.csv (template)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme performance & concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limit options

Hi Marissa \u0014

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming/adding a few details from our side:
- Request mix: ~78% of calls are short (<=200 tokens), ~15% are medium (200\u0013600), ~7% are long (>600) which is where streaming is essential.
- Typical steady-state is 120\u0013160 req/s (US morning peak). We have global users but first pilot will be US-only.
- Bursts: we’ve observed 10\u001320 minute bursts up to ~1,200 req/s during major feature tests. Spikes are typically short but put pressure on concurrent connections.
- Concurrency: our backend will keep up to ~500 active open requests under current app logic; we can explore connection pooling changes on our side.

We’re ok with a 30-day canary. Two asks: 1) can you sketch what the temporary quota bump looks like (numbers + how we’d fall back if we hit a hard cap), and 2) can you confirm streaming behavior for partial failures (if one chunk fails, do you retry the generation or resume?).

I’ll attach a 1-hour sample from last week and a summary CSV for your perf folks (attached).

\u0014Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
Acme Corp
liam@acme.com

Attachments: acme-1hr-sample-20260616.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme performance & concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limit options

Liam \u0014 great, thanks for the data. Looping Dev and Stephanie to propose an initial config and pilot guardrails.

High-level proposal (for discussion):
- Pilot quota: reserved concurrency equivalent to 500 parallel slots for your account, with a burst pool up to 1,200 for 15-minute sliding windows to cover short spikes.
- Rate limits: soft-per-minute token bucket at 75k requests/minute (to smooth microbursts) with hard cap at 1,500 req/s sustained to protect shared capacity.
- Streaming: support chunked responses over HTTP/2. For partial/transport failures we recommend client-side idempotency tokens; server will attempt best-effort resume for transient network errors but long-running generation restarts are treated as new calls. We’ll provide SDK guidance.
- Connection strategy: recommend HTTP/2 multiplexing from edge; we’ll provide headers to set appropriate keep-alive and max-concurrent-streams.

Cost/ops notes:
- Reserved concurrency (500) maps to a Dedicated pool configuration \u0014 I’ve included rough monthly cost estimates in the attached spreadsheet.
- If you want to avoid immediate Dedicated commitment, we can run the 30-day pilot on hosted with a temporary quota increase (trial quota). That will include tight monitoring and a rollback plan.

Action items / next steps:
1) Acme: confirm you’re ok with the pilot quota numbers above (500 reserved / burst to 1,200, soft 75k req/min).
2) Redwood ENG (Dev + Stephanie): run a quick perf validation using Acme sample (attached) and confirm feasibility of burst window and streaming behavior.
3) Ops: if pilot is approved, we’ll provision the temporary quota and share DocuSign link for the SLA amendment.

I’ve attached the proposed-quota-math.xlsx with the back-of-envelope cost model. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical sync this week to walk through how connection pooling/HTTP2 will affect tail latencies.

Thanks \u0014 Marissa

Attachments: proposed-quota-math.xlsx, redwood-slo-options.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme performance & concurrency requirements / Redwood rate limit options

Marissa / team \u0014 quick update from engineering ops after a first pass:
- We can support the 500 reserved concurrency + 1,200 burst for a 30-day pilot on hosted with a temporary quota increase. We'll instrument additional tracing and token-bucket smoothing to monitor tail latency.
- Dev will run the sample through our perf harness today and report back with P95/P99 projections.
- Ops recommends enabling prefix/KV caching for their most common prompt patterns; this should reduce compute and improve P95 in practice.

Marissa \u0014 we can provision the trial quota once Acme signs the amendment. Recommend offering the pilot at no additional hosting charge for the first 30 days; if we see steady sustained >750 reserved usage we\u0014ll convert to a Dedicated recommendation.

\u0014Stephanie
Principal Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference
